name: Chorus Before Hello
why_it_works: Most artist promos open with a pitch; this opens with the best eight seconds of the song. The ear decides in two seconds whether to stay, so leading with the chorus gives the song its only real chance, and the release date rides on a feeling already earned.

hook.pattern: Drop straight into the loudest line of the chorus, title in the first three seconds, no talking.

variables.name: song_title
variables.description: Song title, as sung in the chorus

variables.name: chorus_line
variables.description: The single best chorus line containing the title, capitalized, one breath, 10 syllables or fewer
variables.example: We wore paper crowns and called it gold

variables.name: story_line
variables.description: One honest spoken sentence about where the song came from, capitalized, 12 words or fewer
variables.example: Wrote it in my car after my last shift

variables.name: story_scene
variables.description: The place the song was written, as an object scene with no people
variables.example: a parked car at night with a notebook and phone on the dashboard

beats.purpose: hook: chorus already in, title on screen

visual.prompt: Real performance footage of {{artist_name}} singing full voice, single hard spotlight, vertical crop

beats.purpose: chorus continues with lyric on screen

visual.prompt: Real close-up performance footage of {{artist_name}} mid-note, lyric space in the lower third
Vertical quiet still-life photo of {{story_scene}}, soft practical light, film grain, real and unstaged

music.feel: filtered ambient pad bed under the spoken line, matched to the master's key and tempo

craft.notes: The chorus audio is the artist's own master; the music block only generates the short filtered pad under the spoken story line, so set bpm to the master's real tempo. Start the master one beat before the chorus downbeat so the first syllable the viewer hears is the title, on a stressed beat 1. Choose the chorus line where the title repeats or sits at the end of the phrase; a line with an internal rhyme (crowns / down, gold / told) gives the ear a second hook. Cut to the pad for the spoken line, then slam the master back for the release card. Works best on 90-130 BPM tracks with a big chorus lift.

do_not: Open with 'Hey guys, new song coming out'
Use an intro or verse; only the strongest chorus line earns the first 3 seconds
Describe the song as sounding like a named famous artist
Use an AI-generated version of the artist; real performance footage only
compliance: Artist footage and photos are real and supplied by the artist; never generate the artist's face, body or voice
Use only a master the artist owns or has cleared for ads
